I see so much wireless gear for computers and such. Example: WIFI.

How is this broadcasted and received back again on small antennas. (How the waves are generated is what i am asking.)

Been bugging me for years.
ELI5: How are radio waves are made/received and generally how i can broadcast a message from my Home to a Satellite.
Youtube has some good videos on it.

By sending an electric signal to an antenna with the right length thge signal is transmitted. To recieve a signal there also needs to be an antenna of the same length and amplyfying the signal a lot.

You could theorectcally send a message to a satellite by putting your antanna in a satellide dish. But practically you can't, because it's too expensive to launch communication satellites for hobbyist usage.

Any time you accelerate electrons you generate electromagnetic energy. What this means is that if you move them back and forth at the right timing you can create radio waves. You can alter the frequency of the radio waves by how fast you make the electrons change direction. If the frequncy is between 8.3 kHz (8,300 cycles per second) and 3000 GHz (large number) we call the waves produced radio waves. So, we have electrons moving (which is a current) causing radio waves. If we have them moving in an antenna the waves will spread out, when they hit another antenna they will cause the electrons to move in it. That causes a current that can then be detected and amplified. Different frequencies of radio waves work best with different lengths and shapes of antennas. Something like a commercial radio antenna is designed to send it's signals out across a large area. On the other hand, the spacecraft that just passed Pluto had an antenna designed to focus it's radio signal to as small a point as possible, so it could be detected back on earth. You could send a signal from your home to a satellite if you had a transmitter with enough power and a directional antenna.
